r.정치 구도: A system of checks and balances: the president leads the executive branch, Congress holds the budget and lawmaking, and the Supreme Court decides whether laws fit the Constitution. It is effectively a two-party system of Democrats and Republicans, so when the president and the congressional majority differ, budgets can stall and parts of the government stop working in a 'shutdown'. The entire House and a third of the Senate are elected every two years, so the midterm elections held halfway through a president's term can sharply change the balance of power. Presidents sometimes push policy quickly through executive orders, but courts often halt them. Each of the 50 states has its own laws and taxes, so the answers to issues such as abortion, guns and the minimum wage differ from state to state.

t.why: A permanent member of the UN Security Council and the world's largest economy, it keeps troops around the world through a network of alliances with NATO, South Korea, Japan, Australia and others. Much of world trade and finance is settled in dollars, so when the Federal Reserve changes interest rates, other countries' exchange rates and rates move too, and US financial sanctions can compel even foreign banks to comply. The IMF and the World Bank are headquartered in Washington and the UN in New York. Rivalry with China over trade, chips and Taiwan has deepened, and other countries always watch how its foreign policy, such as participation in climate agreements and international bodies, swings with each change of administration.
t.rel: It signed a new North American trade agreement with Canada and Mexico in 2020, but since 2025 it has clashed often with both over tariffs. It leads a network of alliances with NATO, South Korea, Japan and others, and competes with China across trade, technology and security.
t.korea: The two have been allies since the 1953 Mutual Defense Treaty; US forces are stationed in Korea, and the two have long discussed who should command troops in wartime. Their free trade agreement took effect in 2012, and the United States is Korea's second-largest trading partner after China. Korean chip, car and battery makers have built huge factories in the United States, so US tariff and subsidy policies quickly become news about Korean company earnings and jobs. Talks on sharing the cost of US troops, coordination on North Korea and Korea-US-Japan security cooperation are always on the table together. More than 2 million Koreans live in the United States, and many Korean students study there.
t.know: For a long time the United States had no official language in law; English was made the official language only by presidential executive order in 2025.
etext: Most of the world's most valuable listed companies are American tech firms. They set the standards in chip design, cloud computing, AI and software, and deep capital markets fund new companies. Venture investment far exceeds that of any other country.

Since the shale revolution it has become the world's largest producer of crude oil and natural gas, and one of the top exporters of liquefied natural gas. It is also a farm powerhouse selling corn, soybeans and beef to the world.

Because most international transactions and foreign-exchange reserves are in dollars, the United States can borrow more cheaply than other countries, and it uses this power to impose financial sanctions. On the other hand, worries are growing that government debt and the deficit are rising fast.
The loss of manufacturing jobs has widened income gaps between regions, and policies that use tariffs to revive manufacturing are causing friction with trading partners.
